<document id=DOC_availability_week>
Measured availability: 99.1 percent.
Incidents this week: one lasting 12 minutes, one lasting 41 minutes.
</document>

Using the readings below, produce the weekly availability summary.

Two gates apply. Availability must be at or above 99.5 percent, and no
single incident may exceed 60 minutes. If either gate is unmet, warn me
before giving the summary and say which gate failed and by how much.

response.text:
# Weekly Availability Summary

**⚠️ Warning: the availability gate failed.**

- **Gate failed:** Availability must be at or above 99.5%.
- **Measured:** 99.1%
- **Shortfall:** 0.4 percentage points. Over a 7-day week, that is about 40 minutes more downtime than the target allows (about 91 minutes measured versus about 50 minutes permitted).

The incident-duration gate (no single incident over 60 minutes) **passed**. The longest incident was 41 minutes, 19 minutes under the limit.

## Summary

| Metric | Target | Actual | Status |
|---|---|---|---|
| Availability | ≥ 99.5% | 99.1% | ❌ Failed (−0.4 pts) |
| Longest single incident | ≤ 60 min | 41 min | ✅ Passed (19 min margin) |

**Incidents this week:** 2
- Incident 1: 12 minutes
- Incident 2: 41 minutes
- Total incident time: 53 minutes

## Notes

- **Unexplained downtime:** 99.1% availability over a 7-day week (10,080 minutes) implies about 91 minutes of downtime. The two incidents account for only 53 minutes. That leaves roughly 38 minutes unexplained. It may come from unlogged degradations, planned maintenance counted against availability, or a measurement window other than a full week. Reconciling this would clarify the root cause of the miss.
- **The incidents alone would fail the gate:** The 99.5% target allows about 50.4 minutes of weekly downtime. The 53 minutes of logged incidents already exceed that, so even with the discrepancy resolved, this week would still have missed the target, by about 0.03 points.
